question.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 \\ ∗ & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $D={P}^{-1}AP,$   find the first column of the matrix $P.$

current_example.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/9f4d4fae1174e546876ae1ce443e48a287b5349a40bc4aea4fbfd87e37e2588d.svg) we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_1=5$ and $\lambda_2=-1.$

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda_2=-1.$ 

Now, we simply need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda_2=-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get  

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the corresponding system of linear equations, we construct the augmented matrix $M$ and reduce it to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain $x_1= -{2}x_2.$ Therefore, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/34758f98fad0a6d6ae7db782189813c7109d8f205db763216e2e5b915b1ff21b.svg)

By setting $x_2=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/f27e149b9b262f4a730952385a059368b7ad970cb6d763058ec8e0aae563c594.svg)

Finally, $\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{-2}{1} = -2.$
